name: Hypothesis testing
description: Separate the explanation from its predictions, plan a fair test, and decide what the observed results do and do not support.

walkthroughIntro.inOneLine: Separate the explanation from its predictions, plan a fair test, and decide what the observed results do and do not support.
walkthroughIntro.bestFor: An uncertain explanation that can be challenged by observations or a bounded experiment.
walkthroughIntro.howLong: 31 minutes for 2–6 participants; also available solo.
walkthroughIntro.origin: An independently written workflow using a widely known thinking method. Instructions and fictional examples were created for this app; no third-party endorsement is claimed.

lenses.name: Propose competing explanations
lenses.instruction: Write one tentative explanation and an alternative. State what is already observed and which part is still an assumption.

lenses.name: Make a discriminating prediction
lenses.instruction: Predict an observable difference if your explanation is useful. Name the measure, expected direction and a result that would weaken the explanation. Compare the alternative prediction.

lenses.name: Design the comparison
lenses.instruction: Describe the comparison, assignment or sampling approach, measurement window and decision rule chosen before seeing results. Identify confounders and limits. Use a safe, proportionate test; do not claim a sample is adequate without justification.

lenses.name: Interpret results or record the gap
lenses.instruction: If results exist, record the raw counts or observations, compare them with the prediction and describe uncertainty. If the test has not run, write "Results not yet collected" and identify what to collect; do not invent an outcome.

blocks.title: Agree the question
blocks.prompt: State the observation to explain and the practical decision it affects. Separate existing measurements from impressions.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group agrees the question and boundaries before contributing.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A shared question keeps the later comparisons relevant.

blocks.title: Propose competing explanations

helper.systemPrompt: Coach the participant on this task: Write one tentative explanation and an alternative. State what is already observed and which part is still an assumption. Ask one short question about their own reasoning. Do not supply an answer to their real problem. Separate evidence from assumptions and do not invent results.
helper.hintStyle: Point to one missing piece and ask a concrete question.
examplePool: Fictional practice case — Does a clearer course title help?: Observation: last month 1,200 eligible visitors produced 36 completed signups. Explanation: the vague title hides who the course is for. Alternative: the evening schedule is unsuitable.

walkthrough.whyItMatters: Competing explanations make the test more informative than a search for agreement.

blocks.title: Choose the next step
blocks.prompt: Choose whether to run the test, revise the explanation, or act on existing evidence. State the alternative, prediction, comparison, decision rule, results status and limits.

criteria.text: The explanation, an alternative and a potentially disconfirming prediction are stated.

scoring.zero: No testable prediction or competing explanation is stated.
scoring.one: An explanation and prediction are given, but no alternative or disconfirming result is specified.
scoring.two: An explanation, alternative, and result that would count against the explanation are explicit.

criteria.text: The test names its comparison, measure, window and predeclared decision rule.

scoring.zero: No usable test is described, e.g. see if it improves.
scoring.one: A measure is named but comparison, observation window, or decision rule is missing.
scoring.two: Comparison, measure, observation window and a decision rule set before the test are all explicit.

criteria.text: The conclusion distinguishes observed results from uncollected data and limits its claim accordingly.

scoring.zero: Uncollected outcomes are treated as observed, or the conclusion contradicts recorded results.
scoring.one: The conclusion acknowledges uncertainty but blurs observed and planned results or overgeneralizes.
scoring.two: Actual observations are separated from uncollected data, with conclusions limited to the tested conditions; a planned test claims no result yet.

walkthrough.whatHappens: Participants propose and vote on a conclusion. Review checks the method-specific criteria; solo sessions can use the same checklist.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: A choice should explain its reasoning and limits.

blocks.title: Assign the follow-through
blocks.prompt: Choose an owner, first action, due date and observable success signal.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The group assigns one person the first action and records when and how to check it.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: An owner and a check make the conclusion actionable.

walkthrough.whatHappens: The engine saves the contributions, conclusion and commitment as reports.
walkthrough.whyItMatters: The record makes assumptions and follow-through available for review.
